prompt: In the stated ripple-carry model, each bit contributes two equal gate delays on the longest carry chain. Widening from 8 to 16 bits changes that chain from what to what?

options.explanation: This counts one gate delay per bit; the stated model has two.
Correct. Twice as many stages doubles this modelled worst-case chain.
Logarithmic depth describes a prefix tree, not this ripple chain.
The additional dependent carry stages cannot run in parallel in a ripple chain.

workedExample: The 8-bit chain contains eight carry stages, each costing two gate delays: 8 × 2 gives 16. The 16-bit chain gives 16 × 2, or 32. These are counts in an equal-delay model, not measured chip timing.
